rubrics.justification: The model appropriately stated it could not assess morphology because no image was provided to it and did not fabricate embryo-specific features. It only made general statements about Day 5 blastocysts, so accuracy is good but not a true image-based analysis.
It thoroughly integrated age, ovarian reserve markers, tubal factor diagnosis, endometrial thickness, sperm parameters, BMI, and cycle history into prognosis and transfer planning.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with the implantation estimate tied to age, blastocyst stage, and diagnosis. Minor issues include some overconfident inferences from missing embryo morphology and broad assumptions about euploidy and fresh transfer effects.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice, including SET preference in a good-prognosis young patient and optional PGT-A discussion. Small deviations include advising activity restriction/heavy lifting avoidance after transfer, which is not strongly guideline-based.

It provides practical next steps for luteal support adherence, SET, consideration of PGT-A, and future freeze-all strategy. Some advice is somewhat generic and not tightly tailored to the absent embryo morphology.
